newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-MARKETS HELP COLONIAL TO BUMPER NET.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-MARKETS HELP COLONIAL TO BUMPER NET.

text.p: Newly listed Australian financial services group, Colonial Ltd, on Thursday reported a bumper half-year profit and said it could exceed its forecast for full-year 1997 earnings of A$180 million.

In its first profit report as a listed company, the life insurance, banking and funds management group said its half-year net profit of A$118 million put it on track to meet, or even better, the forecast given to investors in March.
"I am confident we will comfortably achieve or potentially exceed the prospectus forecast," managing director Peter Smedley told a news conference in Melbourne.
Helped by gravity-defying share and bond markets and a crackdown on costs, Colonial's earnings for the six months ended June 30 were already 65 percent of the full-year forecast.
But one share analyst told Reuters a steep fall in investment markets could still put the forecast beyond reach.
"If you had a really bad second half for investment markets, then it's not a given ...," said the analyst who declined to be identified.
Colonial reported growth in new premium business across Australia, New Zealand, Britain and Asia, as well as a drop in the cost of writing these new policies.
Its Colonial State Bank division posted a 22 percent rise in net profit after tax to A$57.1 million, or almost half the group result, partly due to improved efficiency.
The bank's cost-to-income ratio fell to 66.4 percent from 74.1 percent a year ago and operating expenses fell 15 percent.
Operating expenses also fell across the Australian, New Zealand and British insurance and superannuation businesses, by over A$11 million in the half year, Colonial said.
Colonial Investment Management also lowered its costs, and felt a surge of new funds, the group said. The funds manager's assets grew 16 percent to a total of A$22.8 billion, it added.
"The funds management result is a beauty," said HSBC James Capel insurance analyst Nick Caley.
Caley also pointed to lower cost-overruns in writing new insurance business in Australia and Britain as a highlight of the group result. "From what we've seen so far, it looks pretty good," he added.
Investment markets fell in Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines in the half-year but were offset by a strong British bond market and surging share prices in Australia and Hong Kong.
Colonial's total funds held and under management rose to A$43.4 billion at June 30, up 13 percent from December 31.
"This strong result in the current environment reflects the success of Colonial's strategy of diversifying risk away from individual markets," Smedley said.
Shares in Colonial, which listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in May, were 15 cents higher at A$3.55 at 0550 GMT (3.50 p.m.) on Thursday, only four cents short of their record high.
